key_insight: VGGT-Edit enables native, feed-forward 3D scene edits by predicting compact residual fields on top of an existing 3D representation, delivering consistent multi-view changes in a single forward pass.
problem_solved: Brings interactive, instruction-driven editing to generalizable feed-forward 3D reconstruction models by replacing slow, view-by-view or optimization-based edit pipelines that produce inconsistent multi-view results.
method: Predict a residual 3D field (geometry/appearance deltas) conditioned on the input scene and a user edit instruction, then apply it to the base neural 3D representation in one feed-forward step.
Operate natively in 3D (not 2D-lifting), enforcing multi-view consistency and avoiding per-edit optimization loops.
Design the model and training procedure to generalize across scenes so edits can be performed interactively on new environments.
impact: Enables fast, consistent, and user-driven 3D scene editing for interactive applications (e.g., AR/VR content creation, game asset editing, rapid prototyping), reducing latency and engineering overhead compared to optimization-heavy approaches.

paper_title: VGGT-Edit: Feed-forward Native 3D Scene Editing with Residual Field Prediction
paper_authors: Kaixin Zhu, Yiwen Tang, Yifan Yang, Renrui Zhang, Bohan Zeng
